sentences.text:
This appeal is filed by the petitioner seeking enhancement of compensation passed by the MACT,
Vijayapura (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC.No.732/2014 dated 28.02.2017.
2.
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

4. The brief facts of the case are:
On 5.5.2011 at about 9-00 p.m. near Shivalingeshwar Kiran Store, Bhagyanagar cross, Gulbarga, when he was going towards Sedum road on the left side of the road on his motorcycle bearing No.KA-32/X-3563, the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-32/F-1671 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner from opposite side and dashed against the said motorcycle and in the said accident he sustained injuries as shown in the wound certificate.

After the accident he was shifted District Hospital,
Gulbarga.

Thereafter he was shifted to Ganga Institute, Neuro Science Centre,
Trauma Care Hospital, Solapur and he took treatment in the said hospital as an inpatient for a period of one month and undergone operation thrice and incurred medical and other expenses of 24,00,000/-.

entities.text:
Ganga Institute, Neuro Science Centre,
Trauma Care Hospital, Solapur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: After discharge from the 4 Hospital he also has taken treatment on OPD basis in various private Hospitals.
It is stated that the petitioner, prior to the accident he was a student and also doing private service and -getting monthly income of Rs.8,000/-.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner has been permanently disabled and lost source of income.
Thereby causing dent to petitioner financially, mentally and physically.
Hence, he preferred a claim petition seeking compensation.
5. After service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared and filed written statement denying the contents of claim made by the petitioner and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
7. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal after considering the notional monthly income of the claimant awarded compensation of Rs.3,03,000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the quantum of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the present appeal is filed.
9. The learned counsel for the petitioner contended that having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the Tribunal ought to have awarded adequate compensation.
10. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurer supported the judgment and award of the Tribunal and therefore contended that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal be not disturbed.
11. It is seen that the respondents had not challenged the judgment and award and therefore accepted the liability to pay the compensation.
Insofar as claim for compensation is concerned

,
injuries show that petitioner had suffered permanent disability.
The petitioner has not produced any evidence with regard to his income.
Therefore, the notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Since the accident has taken place in the year 2011, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.6,000/- p.m.
The petitioner is aged about 24 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '18'.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,29,600/- (Rs.6,000/- x 12 x 18 x 10%) on account of 'loss of future income'.

12. Considering the nature of injuries, period of treatment, medical bills, I am of the considered opinion that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be re- determined and re-calculated as under:-

02 Towards special and Rs.27,000/- Rs.40,000/-
 diet and attendant  charges  03 Loss of income Rs.17,400/- Rs.17,400/-
duriung
laid up period

04 Towards loss of Rs.25,000/- Rs.40,000/-
 amenities  05 Towards Medical Rs.1,63,378/- Rs.1,63,378/-
 expenses  06 Towards loss of ---- Rs.1,29,600/-
 future earning  Total Rs.3,02,778/- Rs.4,60,378/-
 Rounded off to Rs.3,03,000/-
Praveen Kumar vs The Divisional Controller And Anr on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125085226/
3 13.

In view of the above, I proceed to pass the following;
 ORDER  (a) The appeal is allowed in part.
(b) The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC.No.732/2014 dated 28.02.2017 is modified.
The compensation of Rs.3,03,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.4,60,378/-.
(c) The insurer-respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to the claimant along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
(d) The insurer-respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
(e) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal shall stand intact.

Sd/-
